Key Research Thinking Patterns: Pattern Name: Spatially-Explicit Analysis of Urban Thermal Environment (SETI) - This approach involves the use of geostationary satellite data, remote sensing, and geographically weighted regression (GWR) analysis to identify the spatial patterns and correlations of thermal condition index (TCI) in cities worldwide, and to assess the impact of topography, vegetation cover, and socioeconomic factors on urban thermal environments.

Pattern Name: Machine Learning for Urban Environmental Modeling (MLUEM) - This approach utilizes machine learning algorithms, such as eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP), to investigate the effects of urban form on land surface temperature (LST) and to identify the main contributors to LST variations across local climate zones (LCZs).

Pattern Name: Green Infrastructure Planning and Management (GIPM) - This approach focuses on the impact of internal and surrounding greenspace on local land surface temperature (LST) in built-up LCZs, and aims to provide targeted mitigation strategies for urban heat island mitigation, including transforming old houses or old residential areas into open buildings, using highly reflective building materials or constructing green roofs, and improving the aggregation degree of greenspace patches.

Pattern Name: High-Resolution Data-Driven Urban Planning (HRDUP) - This approach emphasizes the importance of high-resolution data in evaluating urban parks' cooling effects and identifies the underlying causes of overestimation, providing a more robust scientific basis for park planning practices and urban heat adaptation strategies.
Summary Description: Xiangming Xiao is a researcher with expertise in urban planning, environmental science, and geography. His work focuses on the application of remote sensing, geographic information systems (GIS), and machine learning to understand and mitigate the urban heat island effect, promote sustainable development, and improve environmental sustainability. He has developed novel methods for extracting single tree information from RGB satellite images and assessing the impact of greenspace on urban thermal environments. His research has significant implications for climate change adaptation, urban planning, and management, and contributes to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
